proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and suppress the subscript \(x\).  Write
\[
 U=\sum_{i\in\mathcal Y}u_i,
 \qquad
 V=\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y}v_j,
 \qquad
 h=h_x.
\]
A selected--selected coupling is an array \(\gamma=(\gamma_{ij})_{i,j\in\mathcal Y}\) satisfying
\[
 \gamma_{ij}\geq0,
 \qquad
 \sum_j\gamma_{ij}\leq u_i,
 \qquad
 \sum_i\gamma_{ij}\leq v_j,
 \qquad
 \sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}=h.
\]
Its strict-benefit mass is \(n(\gamma)=\sum_{j>i}\gamma_{ij}\).

We first compute the largest mass that can be carried entirely on benefit pairs.  Construct a finite network with a source, one row vertex for each \(i\in\mathcal Y\), one column vertex for each \(j\in\mathcal Y\), and a sink.  Give the source--row arc capacity \(u_i\), the column--sink arc capacity \(v_j\), and include a row--column arc precisely when \(j>i\).  Give each row--column arc the same finite capacity \(M\), where
\[
 M>U+V.
\]
The set of feasible flows is a nonempty compact polytope, so a maximum flow exists.  Its residual network has no source-to-sink path, since augmenting by the minimum positive residual capacity along such a path would increase the flow.  Let \(A\) be the vertices reachable from the source in the residual network.  Every forward arc leaving \(A\) is saturated and every forward arc entering \(A\) carries zero flow.  Summing flow conservation over the vertices in \(A\) other than the source therefore shows that the capacity of the cut \((A,A^c)\) equals the value of the maximum flow.  Since every flow is bounded above by every cut, this reachable-vertex cut is a minimum cut.

The source-only cut has value \(U\).  Hence the reachable-vertex minimum cut has value at most \(U\).  Because
\[
 M>U+V\geq U,
\]
no row--column arc can cross that minimum cut: one such arc would by itself give cut capacity strictly larger than the source-only cut, contradicting minimum-cut optimality.  If \(R\) and \(C\) are respectively the source-side row and column sets, the absence of a crossed benefit arc gives the adjacency implication
\[
 i\in R\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \{j\in\mathcal Y:j>i\}\subseteq C.
\]
If \(R=\varnothing\), deleting every source-side column cannot increase capacity and gives the source-only threshold cut of value
\[
 U=G_K.
\]
If \(R\neq\varnothing\), let \(k=\min R\).  The adjacency implication gives \(j\in C\) for every \(j>k\).  Add to \(R\) every row \(i\geq k\).  This creates no crossed benefit arc because each new row \(i\) is adjacent only to columns \(j>i\), all of which satisfy \(j>k\) and already belong to \(C\); it weakly decreases the cut by removing source--row capacities.  Next delete from \(C\) every column \(j\leq k\).  This creates no crossed benefit arc from the enlarged row set \(\{i:i\geq k\}\), because \(j\leq k\leq i\) contradicts \(j>i\); it weakly decreases the cut by removing column--sink capacities.  The resulting threshold cut has value
\[
 \sum_{i<k}u_i+\sum_{j>k}v_j=G_k.
\]
Conversely, each displayed threshold partition is a cut of that value.  Thus the maximum benefit-only partial-matching mass is
\[
 G^\star=\min_{0\leq k\leq K}G_k.
\]

Repeat the argument for the nonbenefit graph, whose row--column arcs are exactly the pairs \(j\leq i\), again assigning each such arc the same finite capacity \(M>U+V\).  The source-only cut again has value \(U\), so a reachable-vertex minimum cut has value at most \(U\).  Since \(M>U+V\geq U\), no row--column arc crosses this minimum cut.  Its source-side row and column sets therefore satisfy the nonbenefit adjacency implication
\[
 i\in R\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \{j\in\mathcal Y:j\leq i\}\subseteq C.
\]
If \(R=\varnothing\), the source-only threshold cut has value \(U=B_{-1}\).  If \(R\neq\varnothing\), let \(k=\max R\).  Then every \(j\leq k\) belongs to \(C\).  Adding all rows \(i\leq k\) creates no crossed nonbenefit arc, because their neighbors satisfy \(j\leq i\leq k\) and are already in \(C\).  Deleting every column \(j>k\) creates no crossed nonbenefit arc from a row \(i\leq k\).  Both operations weakly decrease cut capacity, and the resulting threshold cut has value
\[
 \sum_{i>k}u_i+\sum_{j\leq k}v_j=B_k.
\]
Conversely these threshold partitions are valid cuts.  Therefore the maximum nonbenefit-only partial-matching mass is
\[
 B^\star=\min_{-1\leq k\leq K-1}B_k.
\]
This is the finite capacitated-cut technique; in both graphs the comparison with the source-only cut, rather than mere finiteness of \(M\), is what excludes crossed row--column arcs.

We now impose total selected--selected mass \(h\).  Any coupling of mass \(h\) carries at most \(B^\star\) on nonbenefit pairs, so
\[
 n(\gamma)\geq h-B^\star,
 \qquad
 n(\gamma)\geq0.
\]
If \(h\leq B^\star\), scale a maximum nonbenefit matching by \(h/B^\star\); when \(h=B^\star=0\), use the zero coupling.  This attains benefit mass zero.  If \(h>B^\star\), take a maximum nonbenefit matching of mass \(B^\star\).  No residual positive-capacity row and residual positive-capacity column can form a nonbenefit pair, because otherwise the matching could be increased along that single edge.  Hence every pair in the product of the positive residual row and column supports is a benefit pair.  The residual row and column totals are \(U-B^\star\) and \(V-B^\star\), and
\[
 U-B^\star\geq h-B^\star,
 \qquad
 V-B^\star\geq h-B^\star
\]
by \(h\leq\min\{U,V\}\).  A greedy allocation between these residual margins therefore adds exactly \(h-B^\star\) units, all on benefit pairs.  Consequently
\[
 n_{\min}=\max\{0,h-B^\star\}.
\]

The same residual-capacity argument with benefit and nonbenefit interchanged shows that a maximum benefit matching can be scaled when \(h\leq G^\star\), while, when \(h>G^\star\), its residual positive row and column supports contain only nonbenefit pairs and can carry the remaining \(h-G^\star\) mass.  Thus
\[
 n_{\max}=\min\{h,G^\star\}.
\]
Convex combinations of lower- and upper-attaining couplings preserve nonnegativity, all row and column capacity inequalities, and total mass \(h\).  Their benefit masses fill the entire interval \([n_{\min},n_{\max}]\).  Substituting the formulas for \(B^\star\) and \(G^\star\), this interval is equivalently characterized by
\[
 0\leq n\leq h,
 \qquad
 n\geq h-B_k\quad(-1\leq k\leq K-1),
 \qquad
 n\leq G_k\quad(0\leq k\leq K).
\]

It remains to complete a selected--selected coupling to the prescribed complier margins over \(\mathcal V\).  Put the unused selected row mass
\[
 u_i-\sum_j\gamma_{ij}
\]
in cell \((i,\bot)\), put the unused selected column mass
\[
 v_j-\sum_i\gamma_{ij}
\]
in cell \((\bot,j)\), and put
\[
 c_x-U-V+h
\]
in cell \((\bot,\bot)\).  The assumed lower bound \(h\geq\max\{0,U+V-c_x\}\) makes the last mass nonnegative, and the row and column capacity inequalities make all other added masses nonnegative.  Because \(\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}u_{xw}=\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}v_{xw}=c_x\) in \(\mathrm{def:diagonal\text{-}residuals}\), the missing row total is \(c_x-U=u_{x\bot}\) and the missing column total is \(c_x-V=v_{x\bot}\).  Hence the completed table has exactly the prescribed margins.  This proves necessity, sufficiency, interval attainability, and missing-category completion.

Fix rational \(q\).  We construct a finite exact chart; no output-sensitive or polynomial-time bound is asserted.  There are finitely many orientations because \(\mathcal O=\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\) and \(\mathcal X\) is finite.  For a fixed orientation \(o\), write the compact formulation of \(Q_o\) after eliminating a maximal fixed independent set of equality rows.  Compactness follows directly from \(\mathrm{def:diagonal\text{-}residuals}\) and \(\mathrm{def:orientation\text{-}polytope}\): each diagonal mass is bounded by an observed mass, the residual margins are affine differences of bounded masses, and \(c_x,f_x,h_x,n_x\) are nonnegative and bounded by those margins.  Thus every nonempty branch is a bounded polytope and has a vertex.

Enumerate every subset of the remaining inequality rows that can supply enough active normals to determine a vertex in the reduced affine space.  The entries of the resulting square systems are polynomials with rational coefficients in \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\).  Indeed, \(\delta_D\) occurs only in the right side of the defier-budget row, \(\delta_S\) occurs only as the coefficient multiplying \(\sum_xc_x\) in the minority-budget row, and every other coefficient is rational when \(q\) is rational.  For an enumerated active set \(I\), let \(D_I(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) be its determinant.  On \(D_I\neq0\), Cramer's rule gives every coordinate of the candidate \(z_I\), and hence \(N_I\) and \(H_I\), as rational functions of the budgets.

These candidates cover every vertex at every budget pair, including degenerate and lower-dimensional parameter values.  At a vertex, the active constraint normals together with the fixed equality normals span the reduced ambient space.  An independent spanning subcollection therefore has nonzero determinant at that parameter value and occurs in the enumeration.  If one determinant vanishes on a singular stratum, it is never used there by continuity; some other nonvanishing active subset represents every vertex that actually exists there.

For completeness, endpoint ratios may be read from the positive-\(H\) vertices.  The constraints \(0\leq n_x\leq h_x\) imply
\[
 0\leq N\leq H.
\]
Let \(z=\sum_v\alpha_v z_v\) be a convex decomposition of a feasible point into branch vertices, with \(\alpha_v\geq0\) and \(\sum_v\alpha_v=1\).  If \(H(z)>0\), then every vertex with \(H(z_v)=0\) also has \(N(z_v)=0\), and
\[
 \frac{N(z)}{H(z)}
 =\sum_{v:H(z_v)>0}
 \frac{\alpha_vH(z_v)}{H(z)}
 \frac{N(z_v)}{H(z_v)}.
\]
The displayed coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one.  Hence the minimum and maximum ratio in a branch occur at positive-\(H\) vertices.  Taking the minimum and maximum over the finitely many orientations gives the global endpoints by \(\mathrm{def:identified\text{-}set}\), \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\), and \(\mathrm{thm:attained\text{-}connected\text{-}endpoints}\).

Clear denominators in every candidate coordinate and slack test.  Form a finite list \(\mathscr P\) of rational polynomials containing: every candidate determinant; every numerator needed to test candidate nonnegativity and all branch inequalities; every numerator needed to test \(H_I>0\); every cross-product needed to compare two candidate ratios after the signs of their positive denominators have been recorded; and the four affine polynomials defining the boundary of \(\mathcal B\).  Partition \(\mathcal B\) by the complete sign vector in \(\{-1,0,1\}^{\mathscr P}\), and discard empty sign classes.  The remaining classes form a finite semialgebraic stratification.  Zero signs retain determinant-zero, equality, singular, and lower-dimensional pieces as actual strata rather than filling them by limits.

On each stratum, for every active set and orientation, the determinant status, feasibility status, and sign of \(H_I\) are fixed.  The stratum therefore receives exactly one of the following mutually exclusive labels:
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \text{model-infeasible},
   &\text{if no branch has a feasible candidate vertex};\\
 \text{model-feasible/target-empty},
   &\text{if a feasible candidate exists but every feasible candidate has }H_I=0;\\
 \text{target-nonempty},
   &\text{if some feasible candidate has }H_I>0.
 \end{array}
\]
These cases are exhaustive and disjoint.  If no feasible candidate vertex exists, no branch can be nonempty because every nonempty compact polytope has a vertex.  If feasible vertices exist but all have \(H=0\), every feasible point has \(H=0\) by convexity and linearity of \(H\).  Conversely, a feasible point with \(H>0\) has a positive-\(H\) vertex in any vertex decomposition.  Thus the second label is exactly model feasibility together with target emptiness, and the third is exactly the domain on which \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\) defines \(L\) and \(U\).

On a target-nonempty stratum, the recorded cross-product signs fix the weak ordering of all feasible positive-\(H\) candidate ratios.  Selecting a least and greatest candidate therefore supplies specified rational formulas for \(L\) and \(U\) throughout that stratum; ties give equal formulas and do not affect the values.  On model-infeasible and model-feasible/target-empty strata, no value of either endpoint is asserted, evaluated, or supplied by continuous extension.

Finally, the finite active-basis table is an exact certificate system.  A feasible vertex is certified by its active set, nonzero determinant, rational coordinate formula, and recorded slack signs.  Model infeasibility is certified by the exhaustive table showing for each potential basis either a zero determinant or a violated constraint.  Model-feasible/target-empty status is certified by one feasible vertex together with the exhaustive \(H_I=0\) signs for all feasible vertices.  On target-nonempty strata, the active basis and cross-product signs certify the endpoint values, and \(\mathrm{prop:sparse\text{-}endpoint\text{-}laws}\), combined with \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\), supplies an attained sparse full-law certificate for each endpoint.  This proves the stated finite rational chart on all regular, singular, and lower-dimensional strata while respecting the domain restriction in \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\).

Fix \(q\).  For a full law with \(H>0\), the causal parameter is \(\theta=N/H\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\), the observed-law functional \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is exactly the set of these causal values over compatible full laws, and, by \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\), \(L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is defined only when that set is nonempty.  Consequently, on the target-existence domain, \(L\geq t\) is equivalent to the causal conclusion that every compatible survivor-complier strict-benefit probability is at least \(t\); it is not a definition of the causal probability.

Let
\[
 \boldsymbol\delta^-=(\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-),
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol\delta^+=(\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)\in\mathcal B
\]
satisfy \(\delta_D^-\leq\delta_D^+\) and \(\delta_S^-\leq\delta_S^+\).  If
\[
 z=(d,u,v,r,s,(c_x)_x,(f_x)_x,(h_x)_x,(n_x)_x)
 \in Q_o(q,\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-),
\]
then every nonbudget constraint in \(\mathrm{def:orientation\text{-}polytope}\) is unchanged at \(\boldsymbol\delta^+\).  Nonnegativity and the two budget rows give
\[
 \sum_x f_x\leq\delta_D^-\leq\delta_D^+,
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_x\{o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x\}
 &\leq\delta_S^-\sum_xc_x\\
 &\leq\delta_S^+\sum_xc_x,
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(c_x\geq0\).  Therefore
\[
 Q_o(q,\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)
 \subseteq Q_o(q,\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)
\]
for every \(o\), and hence
\[
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)
 \subseteq
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)
\]
after restricting to \(H>0\) and applying \(\mathrm{def:identified\text{-}set}\).

Suppose the target exists at \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\) and \(\boldsymbol\delta^+\in\mathcal R_t\).  The larger-budget identified set is nonempty and has lower endpoint at least \(t\).  The preceding inclusion and endpoint attainment from \(\mathrm{thm:attained\text{-}connected\text{-}endpoints}\) imply
\[
 L(q;\boldsymbol\delta^-)
 =\min\Theta_I(q;\boldsymbol\delta^-)
 \geq\min\Theta_I(q;\boldsymbol\delta^+)
 =L(q;\boldsymbol\delta^+)
 \geq t.
\]
Thus \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\in\mathcal R_t\).  The target-existence condition at the smaller budget is essential: initial model infeasibility or target emptiness is excluded by \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}region}\) and is not evidence of robustness.

Now assume \(q\) is rational.  By the corrected \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}rational\text{-}charts}\), every chart stratum is labeled model-infeasible, model-feasible/target-empty, or target-nonempty, and endpoint formulas occur only in the third case.  On a target-nonempty stratum \(\mathcal S_j\), write
\[
 L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\frac{A_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)}{B_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)},
 \qquad B_j\neq0\text{ on }\mathcal S_j,
\]
with rational polynomials \(A_j,B_j\).  Refine by the sign of \(B_j\), and let \(\sigma_j\in\{-1,1\}\) denote that constant sign.  Then
\[
 L\geq t
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sigma_j(A_j-tB_j)\geq0
\]
on \(\mathcal S_j\).  Model-infeasible and target-empty strata are not in \(\mathcal R_t\).  These finite sign tests therefore give an exact semialgebraic description of the robust region.

Take a common sign refinement of all polynomials defining the chart strata, all denominators \(B_j\), all equality polynomials \(A_j-tB_j\), and the facet polynomials of \(\mathcal B\).  On a relatively open cell where none of the relevant polynomials vanishes, both the chart label and the robust-region membership are constant.  The relative boundary of \(\mathcal R_t\) is therefore the finite union of precisely those algebraic sign-cell pieces whose closures meet both \(\mathcal R_t\) and \(\mathcal B\setminus\mathcal R_t\).  This proves the finite piecewise-algebraic boundary claim without a generic-position assumption.

The labels require one further distinction.  An interface between a model-infeasible and a model-feasible piece is a falsification-boundary piece.  Within the model-feasible domain, an interface between a target-empty and a target-nonempty piece is a positive-\(H\) target-existence-boundary piece.  On a target-nonempty stratum,
\[
 A_j-tB_j=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L=t,
\]
so this polynomial certifies the equality locus and nothing more.  Independently, a refined chart piece, whether an equality piece or a formula-interface piece, is a conclusion-boundary piece exactly when its closure meets both \(\mathcal R_t\) and the target-nonempty portion of \(\mathcal B\setminus\mathcal R_t\).  If an equality plateau lies in the relative interior of \(\mathcal R_t\), it fails that closure test and is not a conclusion boundary.  In particular, a stratum on which \(\Theta_I=\{1\}\) and \(t=1\) is a robust equality plateau unless its closure also meets a target-nonempty nonrobust piece.  Because the common refinement retains lower-dimensional intersections, one piece may simultaneously carry any multiple labels whose defining closure tests it satisfies.

Finally fix \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\in\mathcal B\setminus\{\boldsymbol0\}\) and the radial objects in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}region}\).  If \(0\leq\lambda_0\leq\lambda_1\leq1\), then
\[
 \gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_0)
 \leq
 \gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_1)
\]
coordinatewise because both coordinates of \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\) are nonnegative.  Branch feasibility expansion proved above implies that \(\mathcal F_\gamma\) is upward closed.  Restricting the same inclusion to \(H>0\) shows that \(\mathcal E_\gamma\) is upward closed: once a positive-denominator compatible law exists, it remains feasible at every larger point on the path.  If \(\lambda_0\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\), identified-set inclusion yields
\[
 L\bigl(q;\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_1)\bigr)
 \leq
 L\bigl(q;\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_0)\bigr)
 <t,
\]
and target existence persists, so \(\lambda_1\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\).  Hence \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\) is upward closed as well.

The conventions in \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}region}\) now give the stated interpretations.  If \(\mathcal E_\gamma=\varnothing\), no point on the path admits the causal target, so breakdown is inapplicable.  If \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}=\varnothing\), no target-existing point violates the conclusion.  Suppose instead that \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\neq\varnothing\), put \(a=\lambda_{\rm crit}\), and suppose \(a=\lambda_{\rm tar}\) but \(\iota_{\rm crit}=0\).  For every \(\lambda>a\), the definition of the infimum supplies \(b\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\) with \(a<b<\lambda\), and upward closure then gives \(\lambda\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\).  At \(a\) itself no failure is recorded, either because the target is absent there or because its lower endpoint is at least \(t\).  Thus failure occurs immediately after, but not at, the common entry infimum.  When \(a\leq1\), \(\Delta_{\rm crit}=\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(a)\) reports the corresponding budget pair, and \(\iota_{\rm crit}\) reports whether that pair itself belongs to the failure set.

If both \(q\) and \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\) are rational, substitute
\[
 (\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda)
\]
into the finite chart.  Every bivariate rational polynomial sign condition becomes a univariate rational polynomial sign condition.  Its finitely many real roots in \([0,1]\), together with \(0\) and \(1\), partition the path into finitely many points and open intervals on which all chart labels and relevant signs are constant.  Exact root isolation and sign checks therefore determine \(\mathcal F_\gamma\), \(\mathcal E_\gamma\), and \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\), including whether each endpoint is included, and hence determine all three infima, \(\iota_{\rm crit}\), and \(\Delta_{\rm crit}\) when defined.  This is a finite exact evaluation statement, not a scalable or output-sensitive complexity claim.

For \(d\in\{0,1\}\), introduce the proof intermediate
\[
 \widetilde V_d=
 \begin{cases}
 Y_d,&S_d=1,\\
 \bot,&S_d=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:receipt\text{-}consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:selection\text{-}consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\text{-}consistency}\), \(\mathrm{ass:selection\text{-}exclusion}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\text{-}exclusion}\), a unit with response vector \(R\) produces \((D_0,\widetilde V_{D_0})\) under \(Z=0\) and \((D_1,\widetilde V_{D_1})\) under \(Z=1\).  Conditional randomization in \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}randomization}\) and assignment overlap in \(\mathrm{ass:assignment\text{-}overlap}\) therefore identify, within every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the two margins of this pair as the observed masses \(q^0_{xdw}\) and \(q^1_{xdw}\) from \(\mathrm{def:observed\text{-}masses}\).

For the forward projection, represent a response type in cell \(x\) by an arc from its state under \(Z=0\) to its state under \(Z=1\), with mass \(P(X=x,R=r)\).  If \(D_0=D_1=d\), both assignments expose the same treatment-specific state \((d,\widetilde V_d)\), so the arc is diagonal.  Let its mass at state \(w\) be \(d_{xdw}\).  The two margin equations and nonnegativity give
\[
 0\leq d_{xdw}\leq\min\{q^0_{xdw},q^1_{xdw}\}.
\]
The treatment-zero to treatment-one off-diagonal arcs are precisely compliers, with left and right margins
\[
 u_{xw}=q^0_{x0w}-d_{x0w},
 \qquad
 v_{xw}=q^1_{x1w}-d_{x1w}.
\]
The reverse arcs are precisely defiers.  Their treatment-zero and treatment-one state margins are
\[
 r_{xw}=q^1_{x0w}-d_{x0w},
 \qquad
 s_{xw}=q^0_{x1w}-d_{x1w}.
\]
All four residual vectors are nonnegative.  Taking table totals yields
\[
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}u_{xw}
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}v_{xw}=c_x,
 \qquad
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}r_{xw}
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}s_{xw}=f_x,
\]
which are exactly the relations in \(\mathrm{def:diagonal\text{-}residuals}\).

Within the complier table, let \(h_x\) be the mass selected under both treatments.  Since the selected row and column masses are \(U_x\) and \(V_x\), the four selection-response masses for \((S_0,S_1)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\) are
\[
 h_x,
 \qquad U_x-h_x,
 \qquad V_x-h_x,
 \qquad c_x-U_x-V_x+h_x.
\]
Their nonnegativity is equivalent to
\[
 \max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}
 \leq h_x\leq\min\{U_x,V_x\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\), the selected--selected strict-benefit mass \(n_x\) is characterized exactly by
\[
 0\leq n_x\leq h_x,
 \qquad
 n_x\geq h_x-B_{xk}\quad(-1\leq k\leq K-1),
 \qquad
 n_x\leq G_{xk}\quad(0\leq k\leq K).
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{def:selected\text{-}complier\text{-}margins}\) gives
\[
 a_x=U_x-h_x,
 \qquad b_x=V_x-h_x,
 \qquad
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}=\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x.
\]
Choose \(o_x=1\) when \(U_x\leq V_x\), and \(o_x=0\) otherwise.  Then
\[
 o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x=\min\{a_x,b_x\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{ass:selection\text{-}minority\text{-}budget}\) is exactly the branch budget for this orientation, while \(\mathrm{ass:defier\text{-}budget}\) gives \(\sum_xf_x\leq\delta_D\).  Every compatible full law therefore projects into at least one branch \(Q_o\).

For the reverse direction, take a complete reduced array in a fixed \(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\).  For every \(x\), \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\) supplies a selected--selected complier coupling of mass \(h_x\) and benefit mass \(n_x\), together with a completion through \(\bot\) to the full margins \(u_x,v_x\).  This constructs the complier arc table.

The defier margins have common total \(f_x\).  If \(f_x>0\), define
\[
 \rho_x(w_1,w_0)
 =\frac{s_{xw_1}r_{xw_0}}{f_x},
\]
where \(w_1\) is the treatment-one state exposed under \(Z=0\) and \(w_0\) is the treatment-zero state exposed under \(Z=1\).  Division is valid in this case, and direct summation gives margins \(s_x\) and \(r_x\).  If \(f_x=0\), nonnegativity and the margin equalities force \(r_x=s_x=0\), and the zero table has the required margins.  Adjoin the diagonal arcs of masses \(d_{xdw}\).

Every constructed arc determines a response type.  A complier or defier arc specifies both treatment-specific endpoint pairs \((S_0,Y_0)\) and \((S_1,Y_1)\).  If an endpoint is \(\bot\), set the corresponding selection response to zero and assign the unobserved potential outcome an arbitrary fixed element of \(\mathcal Y\).  A treatment-\(d\) diagonal arc specifies the treatment-\(d\) response; fill the never-exposed treatment-\((1-d)\) response arbitrarily.  The arc masses are nonnegative, their arm margins are exactly \(q^0,q^1\), and they total \(p_x\) in cell \(x\) because \(\sum_{d,w}q^z_{xdw}=p_x\).  Give \(Z\) any conditional assignment probability strictly between zero and one and draw it independently of \(R\) given \(X\).  This enforces conditional randomization and overlap without changing the conditional arm margins.  Receipt, selection, and outcome consistency and both exclusions hold by the response-type construction.

The lifted defier mass obeys \(\sum_xf_x\leq\delta_D\).  Its actual minority mass satisfies
\[
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}
 =\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x
 \leq o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x.
\]
Summing and using the branch inequality gives
\[
 \sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}
 \leq\delta_S\sum_xc_x.
\]
Thus the lift lies in \(\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) and has exactly the prescribed \((d,(h_x)_x,(n_x)_x)\).  This proves both projection directions.

To keep the causal target distinct from its identifying functional, define within the proof
\[
 \Theta_I^{\rm causal}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\left\{
 \Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1):
 P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S),
 P\text{ induces }q,
 H(P)>0
 \right\}.
\]
For every such law, the definitions of \(N\) and \(H\) imply
\[
 \Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1)=\frac NH.
\]
The two projection directions, rather than a definition of the causal quantity, therefore prove
\[
 \Theta_I^{\rm causal}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]

For the size claim, introduce per-cell prefixes
\[
 P^u_{x0}=P^v_{x0}=0,
 \qquad
 P^u_{x,k+1}=P^u_{xk}+u_{xk},
 \qquad
 P^v_{x,k+1}=P^v_{xk}+v_{xk}
 \quad(0\leq k\leq K-1).
\]
Then \(U_x=P^u_{xK}\), \(V_x=P^v_{xK}\), and
\[
 B_{xk}=U_x-P^u_{x,k+1}+P^v_{x,k+1}
 \quad(-1\leq k\leq K-1),
\]
with the zero-prefix convention for \(k=-1\), while
\[
 G_{xk}=P^u_{xk}+V_x-P^v_{x,k+1}
 \quad(0\leq k\leq K-1),
 \qquad
 G_{xK}=U_x.
\]
There are \(O(K)\) residual, survivor, benefit, and prefix variables and \(O(K)\) constant-support constraints per cell.  Apart from the two global budget rows, all remaining rows also have constant support per outcome category.  Hence each fixed orientation branch, and only each branch, has \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients.  Its coefficients are integers or entries of \(q,\delta_D,\delta_S\), so they are rational when those inputs are rational.  The union may have up to \(2^m\) branches; no branch-free or scalable \(O(mK)\) positive-budget computation is implied.

At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), nonnegativity and \(\sum_xf_x=0\) force \(f_x=0\), hence \(r_x=s_x=0\), in every cell.  The residual identities then fix
\[
 d_{x0w}=q^1_{x0w},
 \qquad
 d_{x1w}=q^0_{x1w},
\]
and therefore make \(u_x,v_x,U_x,V_x\) observable.  The zero minority budget forces \(\min\{a_x,b_x\}=0\), or equivalently \(h_x=\min\{U_x,V_x\}\), cell by cell.  In the reduced union, the nonnegative branch summands likewise force the orientation to choose the smaller margin, up to ties.  Thus the orientation disjunction collapses to the branch-free exact-mass survivor-complier partial-transport problem, and \(\mathrm{lem:ordinal\text{-}cuts}\) and the lift above give its ordinal cuts, sharp attained endpoints, and full-law completion.

This zero-budget specialization recovers, and is explicitly credited to, the accepted CausalSmith boundary result \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval}\), its full-law lift \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:full-law-endpoint-attainment}\), and its sparse threshold-flow computation \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:linear-sparse-threshold-flow}\), specialization \(\mathrm{v1}\).  The present extension begins at positive \(\delta_D\) and \(\delta_S\): diagonal residuals and defier margins become unknown, both opposing selection responses may coexist within a cell, survivor mass is coupled through the aggregate minority budget, and the exact projection becomes the orientation-indexed disjunctive union proved above.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(t\in[0,1]\), the robust region \(\mathcal R_t\) is relatively downward closed on its target-existence domain: whenever two budget pairs are coordinatewise ordered, the larger lies in \(\mathcal R_t\), and the target exists at the smaller, the smaller lies in \(\mathcal R_t\). proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \(t\in[0,1]\), define
\[
 \mathcal R_t=

For every declared \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\in\mathcal B\setminus\{\boldsymbol0\}\), define the radial path
\[
 \gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda)
 =\lambda\bar{\boldsymbol\delta},
 \qquad 0\leq\lambda\leq1,

and the three subsets of \([0,1]\)
\[

 \mathcal F_\gamma
 &=\left\{\lambda:\bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}

 \neq\varnothing\right\},\\
 \mathcal E_\gamma

 \Theta_I\bigl(q;\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda)\bigr)

 \Delta_{\rm crit}
 =\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_{\rm crit}).
\]

prose_updates.tldr: With randomized binary assignment, endogenous receipt, and an ordinal outcome observed only after post-treatment selection, the positive defier and selection-minority budgets yield an exact finite union of orientation-specific rational threshold-cut polytopes, and every reduced point lifts to a compatible full law. Each branch, not the whole disjunctive problem, has \(O(mK)\) size. The scalar sharp set is an attained interval; finite all-bases charts label model infeasibility, model-feasible target emptiness, and target-nonempty endpoint formulas without extending \(L\) or \(U\) through \(H=0\). Radial reports distinguish model entry, target entry, and actual conclusion failure. At \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\), the construction recovers the branch-free partial-transport projection, ordinal cuts, full-law lift, sharp endpoints, and sparse threshold-flow computation already proved in the accepted CausalSmith paper \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\). The new extension is the positive-budget regime with unknown diagonal residuals and defiers, within-cell coexistence of opposing selection responses, a budget-coupled survivor mass, and an orientation-indexed union. Output-sensitive chart enumeration remains open.

project_justification.gap: The accepted CausalSmith paper \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\) already closes the no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection boundary with a branch-free partial-transport projection, ordinal threshold cuts, full-law lifting, sharp attained endpoints, and sparse linear-time threshold flow. Published selected-complier and ordinal-benefit analyses do not supply the positive-budget combination of treatment defiers, within-cell opposing selection responses, an aggregate minority-selection budget, and a survivor denominator that may be absent.
project_justification.niche: The remaining mathematical niche is therefore the joint-violation surface at positive \(\delta_D\) and \(\delta_S\): diagonal residuals and defier margins are unknown, both selection directions may coexist in each covariate cell, and survivor mass is coupled across cells by the minority budget. Target existence must be separated from both model feasibility and robustness.
project_justification.fill: The projection and reverse lift reduce compatible full laws exactly to a finite orientation-indexed union whose individual branches have \(O(mK)\) extended size. Attained endpoints, sparse full-law certificates, finite rational charts, closure-correct boundary labels, and exact radial critical-budget reports follow. At zero budgets the formulas specialize to, and explicitly credit, the accepted branch-free boundary result; no new zero-budget algorithm is claimed.

prose_updates.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith paper \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\), through \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval}\), \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:full-law-endpoint-attainment}\), and \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport/thm:linear-sparse-threshold-flow}\), already establishes the branch-free survivor-complier partial-transport projection, ordinal threshold cuts, full-law lifting, sharp attained endpoints, and sparse \(O(|\mathcal X|K)\) computation on the no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection boundary. That boundary is the finite-ordinal Dong--Heiler anchor under their conditional-first-stage and assignment-overlap support convention. The present result recovers it at \((0,0)\) and extends the model only at positive budgets, where defier residuals are unknown, opposing selection responses coexist within cells, survivor mass is coupled by an aggregate budget, and an orientation disjunction is unavoidable. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen study ordinal benefit without this post-treatment-selection denominator. Bartalotti, K\'edagni, and Possebom use a latent-index treatment rule and monotone-selection refinement that exclude the violations admitted here. Masten and Poirier motivate two-assumption conclusion frontiers, while Picchetti supplies a defier-share sensitivity coordinate; neither separates model entry, survivor-target entry, and conclusion failure. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski motivate symbolic parametric-optimization tools but do not deliver a degeneracy-safe output-sensitive enumerator for this disjunctive rational chart.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The proved symbolic construction is finite all-bases enumeration, including singular and lower-dimensional strata; it is not output-sensitive. Positive-budget \(O(mK)\) size holds per orientation branch only, and as many as \(2^m\) branches may remain. The early kill test must still reproduce the explicit binary surface, the opposite-orientation witness, and the vanishing-denominator example with exact equality and empty-target strata, endpoint full-law certificates, and an audit excluding hidden exponential rejected-basis work. Failure of that computational test does not affect the projection, pointwise endpoint, chart-existence, or radial-characterization theorems.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves the ordinal-cut characterization, exact positive-budget full-law projection and lift, attained connected endpoints, sparse endpoint laws, finite rational charts with endpoints only on target-nonempty strata, closure-correct breakdown labels, exact radial entry and critical-budget reports, simultaneous finite-sample outer coverage, and the zero-budget reduction. The branch-free zero-budget projection, lifting, sharp endpoints, and sparse threshold-flow algorithm are credited to the accepted \(\texttt{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport\_v1}\) result and are recovered here rather than claimed as new. The \(O(mK)\) formulation bound is per orientation branch; no branch-free, polynomial, strongly polynomial, scalable, or output-sensitive positive-budget algorithm is claimed. Equality loci \(L=t\) are not called conclusion boundaries unless their closures meet both robust and target-nonempty nonrobust pieces. Pre-feasibility and pre-target portions of a radial path are not robustness. The output-sensitive degeneracy-safe enumerator, regular endpoint inference at ties, and empirical reanalysis remain outside scope.
